proof_scope: WebGPT-authored adversarial Tau trust-boundary evals. These cases are intentionally not tuned to current validators; failing cases are expected evidence of missing hardening, not a fixture defect.

claims.proves: The fixture executes the real $ask preflight path for underspecified requests and Tau's public DAG runner for WebGPT-designed malicious DAG and receipt payloads, then reads back generated case receipts.
claims.does_not_prove: Live browser semantic quality, real provider identity under production load, real human acceptance, or closure of the WebGPT-identified hardening gaps until the adversarial cases pass. Fault-injected deterministic cases are not labeled real_world.

what_was_exercised: local commands declared in the fixture manifest
what_remains_unverified: semantic correctness, live services, LLM judge behavior, and release readiness

claims.description: Tau fails closed across WebGPT-identified local trust boundaries: forged receipts, stale lineage, verifier bypass, join forgery, human acceptance forgery, provider metadata laundering, and proof laundering.
$ask refuses underspecified Tau DAG requests instead of using agent-authored context as human intent.
